title: Light bleeding around ovulation
answer: A few people notice a small amount of pink or brown spotting around the middle of their cycle, at about the time of ovulation. If the bleeding is heavier, lasts longer, comes with pain or bad-smelling discharge, or happens after sex, see a health worker to be checked.

title: Stress and periods
answer: Stress affects the part of the brain that controls your period hormones. During times of worry, such as exams, family problems, moving home or grief, your period may come late, early, be lighter, heavier, or even skip a month. Usually, periods return to normal when stress eases. Sleep, exercise, talking with someone you trust and making time to relax can help. If periods stay irregular or stress feels too much, talk to a health worker or call 114.

If you are trying to lose weight, feel afraid of eating, or your periods have stopped, please talk to a health worker.

title: What endometriosis is
answer: Endometriosis is a long-term condition where tissue similar to the womb lining grows outside the womb, for example on the ovaries or in the pelvis. This tissue can cause pain, especially around periods. It can start in teenage years, but it often takes time to be recognised. It is not caused by anything you did, and it is not an infection. It can be managed, so if you have strong period pain, talk to a health worker.

title: What PCOS is
answer: PCOS (polycystic ovary syndrome) is a common hormone condition where the ovaries do not release eggs regularly and the body may make more of the hormones usually found in higher amounts in males. It can affect periods, skin, hair and weight. The word cyst can sound scary, but these are small fluid sacs, not cancer. PCOS can be managed with healthy habits and treatment from a health professional.

title: What fibroids are
answer: Fibroids are growths made of muscle in or on the wall of the womb. They are not cancer. They are common in adult women, especially from their thirties onward, and are rare in teenagers. Many cause no problems, but some can cause heavy or long periods, pain, a swollen belly or needing to pee often. If your mother or another woman has fibroids, a health professional can explain the treatment options for her.

title: Can period products cause infertility
answer: No. Pads, cloth pads, tampons, menstrual cups and period underwear do not cause infertility or damage your womb when used and cleaned properly. They only collect blood. What matters is hygiene: change products regularly, keep reusable ones clean and dry, and follow time limits for tampons and cups. If you notice pain, itching, or a bad smell, see a nurse, but using these products will not stop you having children.

title: Is period blood dirty
answer: Period blood is not dirty, impure or dangerous. It is made of blood and womb lining and is as clean as blood from any other part of the body.
